A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same set-based reinforcement learning work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, allowing content to be matched despite substantial reorganization and formatting changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original control experiments, including verified-return curves, adversarial-attack evaluations, training runtimes, and the appendix's 2D quadrocopter results.

after.justification: v2 retains original control experiments and reports additional baseline comparisons, verification-toolbox evaluations, Hopper-v2 experiments, and hyperparameter studies.

M1.justification: The SA-SC and SA-PC procedures retain zonotope propagation, the center-error plus diameter regression loss, weighted set-based policy gradients, and the actor-only simplification. The gradient factors are rearranged equivalently, and the expanded exposition does not establish a new method component or training procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds MuJoCo Hopper-v2 locomotion, substantially extending evaluation to more complex dynamics and larger state/action spaces. The original navigation, inverted-pendulum, and 1D/2D quadrocopter tasks remain; 'quadrotor' is a renaming, and the 2D task was already evaluated in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: v1 compares against PA-PC, Naive, and Grad. v2 adds evaluated MAD and RORL comparators in Figure 5, broadening comparison to maximum-action-difference attacks and conservative smoothing. RORL is explicitly excluded from the TD3 comparison; the appendix's 2D quadrotor plot retains the original comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 introduces verification across four toolboxes and empirical Hopper evaluation using 50 MAD-attacked trajectories and 200 trajectories with uniform perturbations. It also adds noiseless learning-curve evaluations. The reported verified-return formula changes its negative-reward sign convention from v1 Equation 30 to v2 Equation 12. Existing network sizes and tabulated training hyperparameters remain unchanged; newly stated horizons do not establish changed settings.

E4.justification: Beyond the existing weighting-factor comparisons and quadrocopter attack analysis, v2 adds actor/critic regularization sweeps with convergence histories, learning curves, verification-toolbox dependence tests, and attack-specific results for the inverted pendulum. These examine parameter sensitivity, training stability, and whether improved verifiability extends beyond CORA.

E5.justification: v1 states that experiments use five seeds and displays shaded bands without defining their statistical meaning. v2 explicitly reports means and 95% confidence intervals across five seeds. This improves uncertainty reporting without establishing an increase in the number of runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds MAD/RORL results, Hopper returns and runtimes, sensitivity and convergence results, and multi-toolbox verification outcomes. Table 1 reports CORA verification times of 423.45 seconds for the standard agent and 1.99 seconds for the set-based agent. The retained attack-return plots are also revised between v1 Figure 6 and v2 Figure 7. The original training-time values remain unchanged in v2 Table 2.

T1.justification: The central loss derivations and expectation-preservation proof are retained, largely in v2 Appendix B. v2 adds a polynomial runtime bound and proof in Proposition 4, formulates the objective using adversary-dependent state visitation, explicitly restricts the expectation-preservation proposition to ReLU networks, and revises the sign in the verified-return expression. These are bounded additions and corrections to the existing theoretical framework.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains set-based reinforcement learning for verifiably robust control. v2 additionally claims verifiability across different frameworks and quantifies perturbation tolerance as up to nine times that of standard reinforcement learning. It also explicitly claims empirical scalability to more complex locomotion tasks, extending rather than replacing the original contribution.

C2.justification: v1 discusses conservative policies and computational costs. v2 adds substantive qualifications: training alone does not guarantee robustness, Hopper results lack formal certification, verification requires known dynamics and bounded uncertainties, and model mismatch can invalidate safety guarantees. Appendix C also interprets how critic regularization affects contraction and convergence, expanding the explanation of the robustness-performance trade-off.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies benchmark time horizons, averaging over the last five agents in each training run, Hopper evaluation details and hardware, and code/video access pointers. The existing architecture and training-parameter table are retained. These additions improve documentation without demonstrating changes to the corresponding retained experimental settings.

R1.justification: The basic positioning against pointwise adversarial training remains. v2 adds discussion and citations concerning conservative smoothing, randomized smoothing, model-based certification, alternative verification tools, and reachset-conformant modeling. Much of the dedicated related-work section relocates earlier introductory material; Koller et al.'s preprint-to-publication update is the same underlying work.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, method explanations, and evaluation narrative. It moves the probabilistic derivations into Appendix B, consolidates benchmark descriptions in Appendix C, brings the regression-loss proof into the main text, and introduces dedicated related-work and limitations sections. The presentation now emphasizes gradient sets and verified performance.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column layout to a predominantly single-column journal layout. v2 adds set-propagation and gradient illustrations, verification and Hopper runtime tables, and numerous sensitivity and learning-history plots. Existing experimental figures are enlarged or restructured, while the probability-density illustration and 2D quadrotor results are relocated and relabeled.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the central verifiability claim through additional robust-RL baselines, verification across four toolboxes, and sensitivity and convergence studies. Explicit confidence intervals and substantive limitations make the evidence easier to assess, especially the distinction between empirical Hopper robustness and formal certification. The Hopper runtime caption understates overhead—Table 4 reports 343.56 versus 44.70 seconds for SA-PC and PA-PC—but this limited weakness does not outweigh the substantial gains in validation and qualification.
